title: 2 failed attempts, video call: How 'Rs 1.2 crore testicle' claim led to teen's murder
content: A 16-year-old boy was murdered in Bhopal by a group believing his testicles were valuable. The alleged mastermind was inspired by a social media hoax about organ prices. Police recovered the decomposed body and confirmed the removal of body parts. Divers are searching two lakes for the missing organs as evidence. The accused posed as a doctor to convince associates of the false plan.

title: Manav Suthar's ten-wicket haul floors Sri Lanka as India conquer Galle challenge
content: Manav Suthar's second Test five-for and Devdutt Padikkal's maiden century powered India to a crushing 165-run win over Sri Lanka in in the first Test Galle. The young left-arm spinner stamped his authority on a dramatic second session, picking up three wickets in an over to wrap up Sri Lanka's second innings quickly.

title: Cabinet clears 4 railway projects worth Rs 9,450 crore across 4 states: Key details
content: The Union Cabinet greenlit five significant infrastructure initiatives totaling over thirteen thousand crore rupees. Among these, four railway multitracking projects will extend the network by four hundred ten kilometers, alleviating congestion and enhancing freight transport across various states. Additionally, an NH-22 highway upgrade project in Bihar will improve the eighty-two kilometer stretch, bolstering connectivity with the Nepal border.

title: US tech firm asks court to block CEO who fired 900 in 79-second call
content: Better Home & Finance is suing former CEO Vishal Garg in a US court. The company seeks to block Garg from gathering shareholder support for his return. Garg allegedly violated securities laws by making misleading statements to regain his position. The board unanimously removed Garg after significant company losses and stock decline. Garg seeks reinstatement, offering to work for one dollar annually.

title: Navi Mumbai road rage: Ola driver thrashed, dragged 2km on car bonnet
content: A road rage incident in Nerul involved an Ola cab driver being assaulted. The cab driver was struck with a bamboo stick, causing severe head injuries. He then lay on the car's bonnet to prevent the attacker's escape. The accused car driver sped away with the injured man on the hood. Police have registered an FIR and are searching for the absconding driver.

title: Russia turns to Asia for refined fuel, set to receive nearly 270,000 tonnes in Aug
content: Russia is importing refined fuel from Asian nations this month. Ukrainian attacks on its oil refineries have reduced domestic fuel production significantly. India supplies about one-third of these crucial refined fuel imports. These shipments use ship-to-ship transfers to obscure their origins. Russia has also tightened its own fuel export curbs to manage shortages.

title: US issues details of new Green Card rules coming into effect from September 18
content: Starting September 18, 2026, new regulations from the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services will affect Green Card applications, implementing a more rigorous public charge test. This means applicants will be assessed more thoroughly regarding any public benefits received. However, existing Green Card holders and certain humanitarian cases will not be subject to these enhanced evaluations.

title: Meet Kanav Jain, student who built low-cost aircraft to deliver medicines
content: Kanav Jain, a talented Scottish student, has been awarded the prestigious UK Young Engineer of the Year for creating AeroAid, an innovative low-cost autonomous drone aimed at delivering medical supplies. This versatile VTOL quadplane combines the best features of helicopters and airplanes, making it ideal for reaching remote locations. Jain’s mission is to leverage technology for vital humanitarian assistance, reflecting his commitment as a leader in drone technology workshops.

title: US released weevil to fight musk thistle; it later attacked 25 native thistles
content: A biological control initiative aimed at managing invasive thistles integrated a weevil specifically targeting musk thistle. Unfortunately, this insect extended its reach to native plant species, leading to detrimental effects on local thistles, including an endangered variety that experienced a decline in seed production. This situation underscores the critical importance of careful evaluation in invasive species control programs.

title: Netflix cofounder Reed Hastings to CEOs: Stop calling your teams family
content: Reed Hastings, co-founder of Netflix, cautions executives against labeling their organizations as families. He advocates for a championship team mentality, which not only promotes superior performance but also adapts to change effectively. Referencing his own experience during Netflix's layoffs in 2001, Hastings reinforces his point, joined by other executives, including Brian Chesky and Tobi Lütke, who support this perspective on talent management.

title: Manav Suthar creates history: Youngest Indian to take 10-wicket haul in away Test
content: Manav Suthar became the youngest Indian to take ten wickets in an away Test. His performance secured India's victory against Sri Lanka in Galle. Suthar joined an elite group of Indian spinners with this achievement. Captain Shubman Gill praised the young bowler's promising future contributions. This win earned India crucial World Test Championship points.

title: Zepto’s alleged 20-kg internship rule sparks gender bias row, debate online
content: The alleged Zepto internship advertisement has triggered a debate over gender, physical requirements and fairness in campus hiring. The purported notice, offering Rs 20,000 monthly, reportedly sought male students while requiring candidates to lift 20 kg and stand for 10–12 hours. As questions mount over the role’s authenticity, the controversy highlights concerns surrounding transparent and equitable recruitment practices.

title: SL batter says 'thank you' to Jaiswal's 'IPL' promise, then throws his wicket
content: With Sri Lanka chasing 372, Dickwella and Jaiswal exchanged words during the 60th over, with Jaiswal challenging the left-hander to attack India's bowling.

title: China becomes first to recover orbital rockets using two methods: How Zhuque-3 works
content: China's LandSpace company achieved a significant milestone in reusable rocket technology. The Zhuque-3 rocket's first stage successfully landed vertically on land after launch. This achievement demonstrates a key step towards reducing space launch costs for China. The successful recovery follows modifications after a previous mission's failure. This development supports China's expanding satellite internet ambitions and global space market competition.

title: Bus takes a different route, passenger misses flight; gets Rs 73k payout
content: A consumer commission ordered Greenline Travels to pay compensation for a significant delay. The bus company's route deviation caused a passenger to miss his flight to Delhi. The complainant was pursuing an M.Phil. and needed to reach Delhi for his course. The commission found the company deficient in service for the unexplained delay. Greenline Travels must pay Rs 73,000 for flight, accommodation, and mental agony.

title: 9-yr-old girl sexually assaulted, murdered in Pune; neighbour held
content: A nine-year-old girl was allegedly assaulted and murdered in Pune district. The incident occurred Tuesday afternoon in Junnar tehsil, police reported. A 25-year-old man has been taken into custody by authorities. He allegedly took the child from her home to a nearby farm. A case has been registered, and further investigation is ongoing.

title: Rabb Se Hai Dua's Amrapalli Gupta alleges bad behaviour from co-star Dheeraj Dhoopar
content: Amrapalli Gupta has expressed that Dheeraj Dhoopar's consistent tardiness disrupted the filming schedule for their show. This resulted in delays for both script readings and lunch breaks, causing frustration among the cast and crew. Gupta believes these ongoing issues may have played a role in the show's eventual cancellation, underscoring the need for all artists to honor each person's time on set.

title: 'Our problems needn't be resolved in Washington': Abdullah on US envoy's J&K visit
content: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah stated that India's central government will resolve regional problems. He emphasized that Washington would not be involved in addressing these issues. US Ambassador Sergio Gor is visiting Jammu and Kashmir for the first time. The envoy will also likely meet Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha. Gor's visit holds significance given his role as Special Envoy.

title: TN property registration goes online for first sale: What you need to know
content: Tamil Nadu now requires online registration for initial property sales. This new system eliminates physical visits to sub-registrar offices for buyers and developers. Builders and applicants must create logins on the TNREGINET portal for document submission. Executants, claimants, and witnesses will provide Aadhaar and biometric authentication online. Registering officers must process applications within twenty-four hours of submission.

title: India becomes the least-favoured Asian stock market in BofA survey - here's why
content: The survey identified the absence of clear exposure to artificial intelligence as the biggest concern for Indian equities, followed by weak economic growth. As many as 32% of respondents were net underweight on India.

title: Netanyahu's party puts Mamdani alongside Iran, Hezbollah leaders on billboard
content: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's party placed Mayor Mamdani's image on a billboard.  This billboard featured Mamdani alongside leaders hostile to Israel's interests.  Netanyahu is campaigning for re-election amid political challenges in Israel.  He has increasingly used Mamdani's criticism as campaign messaging.  The exchange occurs while Gaza ceasefire efforts remain stalled.

title: Taunts over looks, IQ not enough to invoke Section 498A: Jharkhand HC
content: The Jharkhand high court quashed a criminal case against a man accused of cruelty.  The court found the allegations did not meet Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.  Taunts about complexion and low IQ were deemed insufficient to constitute cruelty.  The court stated continuing the case would be an abuse of legal process.  Therefore, the criminal proceedings against the petitioner were set aside.

title: Abhishek Bachchan reveals why he chose Jaipur Pink Panthers
content: In a recent interview, Abhishek Bachchan revealed the heartfelt journey behind his kabaddi team, proudly rooted in his personal life. He chose Jaipur for its sentimental value, infusing the team’s identity with his daughter’s beloved color. His active role in shaping the team during its foundational days was key to its progress. The attendance of high-profile celebrities during the team’s debut match significantly elevated the sport's profile.

title: ‘When I was at my lowest’: PV Sindhu reveals Kohli’s message during career low
content: PV Sindhu opened up about her strong friendship with Virat Kohli, whom she regards as a brother figure. During a challenging time in her career, Kohli provided her with invaluable guidance, encouraging her to embrace her authentic playing style. This heartfelt exchange transformed Sindhu's outlook on overcoming hurdles, and she remains inspired by Kohli's achievements as they learn from one another.

title: Who is Satyaki Savarkar? Family tree, political links & Rahul Gandhi case explained
content: Satyaki Savarkar, V.D. Savarkar's grandnephew, is the complainant in a defamation case.  Rahul Gandhi faces charges for alleged remarks made about Savarkar in London.  Satyaki's family links to both Savarkar and Godse families have emerged during cross-examination.  The court is considering a plea for Rahul Gandhi's voice sample for forensic comparison.  Proceedings continue as the court awaits a formal response from the defence.

title: IAS Singham Tukaram Mundhe: From a village school to 25 transfers, his journey
content: ‘IAS Singham’ Tukaram Mundhe is back in the spotlight with his strict crackdown on food safety violations as Maharashtra FDA Commissioner. From studying at a Zilla Parishad school in Beed to securing AIR 20 in UPSC, his journey reflects a remarkable rise. With over two decades in administration and around 25 transfers, Mundhe remains a closely watched officer.

title: 'Voice sample not required': Rahul's counsel opposes plea in Savarkar defamation case
content: Rahul Gandhi's lawyer opposed a plea for his voice sample in a defamation case. The defense argued the request was premature for the ongoing court proceedings. Satyaki Savarkar's deposition also brought Godse-RSS links into focus during cross-examination. The defamation case stems from remarks made by Rahul in London during 2023. The court has directed the defense to file its formal response by September 1.

title: 'Wasn't I anti-national for you?' Dipke on offer to join NDA camp

Athawale invited Dipke, describing him as an active Ambedkarite, to strengthen society and the party. The Union minister also mentioned a potential Union cabinet reshuffle happening very soon. He urged eight NCP (SP) MPs to join the NDA government if Sharad Pawar declines.

title: Middle East war: Indian refiners forced to buy oil at premium; Russian discounts vanish

title: Inside Vivek Oberoi’s Mumbai home: Goan farmhouse charm and pet cow Kamadhenu
content: Vivek Oberoi's home in Mumbai is a serene escape, echoing the charm of Goan farmhouses. Adorned with antique furnishings and natural accents, the space embodies his essence. A beloved pet cow, Kamadhenu, enhances the earthy vibe. This intimate refuge starkly contrasts with his public persona, offering a genuine glimpse into his life. The design embraces uniqueness and seamlessly merges indoor and outdoor spaces, giving it a lived-in feel.

title: Joe Root on the verge of history, Ricky Ponting’s all-time record in sight
content: Joe Root, the captain of England, is set to take on Pakistan at Headingley beginning Wednesday. He requires seventy-nine runs to eclipse Ricky Ponting's esteemed home Test record and is striving to become England's highest run-scorer at Headingley. With just a stone's throw from twelve thousand international runs accumulated on English grounds, this series signifies an important evolution in English cricket.

This decision may also be linked to tensions concerning Iran and US-South Korea ties.

title: J&K Pharmacy Students Face Eviction Pressure In Bhopal, Cops Probe Claims
content: The Jammu & Kashmir Students Association (JKSA) raised the matter in a three-page letter to Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Tuesday, seeking his "immediate and personal intervention"

title: Vijay rolls out slew of perks for TN MLAs: Car, monthly allowances, increased health cover
content: all members of the legislative assembly will be provided government vehicles . each MLA will receive a monthly vehicle allowance of Rs 75,000 to cover the driver's salary and car-related expenses . an additional Rs 25,000 per month will be given to each member to hire an assistant .

title: 'Because Punjab election is coming up': Satyendar Jain cries foul after arrest
content: alleged irregularities in the Delhi Jal Board's (DJB) tendering process . the arrest of the loyalist came a day earlier in connection with alleged DJB scam . former chief minister and aAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal has also questioned the arrest .

title: Pakistan govt to challenge SC order to move jailed ex-PM Imran Khan to hospital
content: the pakitan supreme court ordered the transfer of jailed former prime minister to a private hospital within two days . the move could end hopes of imran Khan’s family and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) who have repeatedly sought better treatment .

title: 'Foolproof system, difficult to breach': Centre lists NEET security measures before SC
content: the Centre told the Supreme Court that the system in place for conducting the NEET examination is “foolproof” and difficult to breach . the centre said vehicles carrying NEET question papers are equipped with GPS systems and their movements, including even minor deviation, are recorded .

title: 'He would get corruption done': Maliwal targets Kejriwal after Satyendar Jain's arrest
content: former chief minister arvind Kejriwal accused of presiding over a decade of corruption . he allegedly allowed corruption to be carried out through ministers, which he later blamed . she also alleged that thai party leader Satyendar Jain was acting as a “collection agent” for thursday .

title: Bihar: Water cannon used as RJD leaders march to Raj Bhavan; Tejashwi, Misa detained
content: AK-47 rifles were used against students protesting over paper leak issue . a foot march was held in patna towards Raj Bhavan . the march raises concerns over papers leaks, unemployment and issues affecting students and youth .

title: Iran claims control, ships choose Omani route: What's changing in Strait of Hormuz
content: the battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz has emerged as a key focus of the Iran war . the competing claims have created uncertainty over the extent of control exercised by either side over the critical waterway . however, shipping data indicates that the united states is gaining ground as its navy patrols the strait .

title: Vijay govt revokes order barring students from Left, CJP protests in Tamil Nadu
content: TN govt rolls back order to prevent students and youth from joining political protests and agitations . the measures were aimed at programmes organised by left-wing parties and the Tamil Nadu Cockroach Janta Party .

title: 'There's a problem at the border': Rijiju admits delineation confusion in Arunachal
content: union minister says there is a problem at the border but only because the boundary has not been delineated . concerns raised by villagers in the frontier state are valid, but warned against spreading misinformation about Chinese troops entering Indian territory .
